extracted.intended_audience: members of the public (landowners, Tribes, environmental groups), federal/state/local agencies, and other interested parties invited to participate in FERC's NEPA scoping and supplemental EIS process
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting scoping comments for FERC's supplemental Environmental Impact Statement (SEIS) for the Rio Grande LNG Terminal and Rio Bravo Pipeline projects, following the Commission's procedural and substantive guidance. Includes how to submit comments, what issues to address, and criteria the SEIS will use to evaluate alternatives and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline (scoping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments so that the Commission receives them in Washington, DC on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 15, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure comments are timely and properly recorded, meet this deadline; comments received after the deadline may not be considered in the scoping record for the supplemental EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods: (1) eComment feature on FERC website for brief, text-only comments; (2) eFiling on FERC website to attach files (new users must create an account via eRegister and select 'Comment on a Filing'); (3) paper copy mailed to the Acting Secretary at the addresses provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is encouraged; staff assistance is available at (866) 208-3676 or FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov. Follow the instructions carefully so comments are properly recorded. Paper submissions must reference the project docket numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference docket numbers in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must reference the project docket numbers (CP16-454-000; CP16-455-000; and/or CP20-481-000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mailing paper comments, include the docket numbers on your letter and send to the specified addresses. Include docket numbers in electronic filings as directed so the comments are associated with the correct project record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of scoping comments (focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission requests public comments on the scope of issues to address in the supplemental EIS and asks commenters to focus on issues that may have a significant effect on the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your comments will help Commission staff focus its analysis on significant issues. Provide specific input on additional issues or alternatives to be analyzed in the supplemental EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues the supplemental EIS will analyze (court-identified focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental EIS will focus on the issues identified by the court as requiring further analysis: environmental justice impacts, air quality impacts (construction and operational emissions), and an updated alternatives analysis (including carbon capture and sequestration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEIS will tier off the staff's April 26, 2019 final EIS and provide updated analyses and recommendations on how to lessen or avoid impacts. Comments relevant to these topics are directly responsive to the court's remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives evaluated in the SEIS must be reasonable, technically and economically feasible, and meet the purpose and need for the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing alternatives (including alternative facility sites and pipeline routes), focus on those that meet project objectives, are technically and economically feasible, and that avoid or lessen environmental impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives currently under consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEIS will evaluate the no-action alternative (project not implemented) and carbon capture and sequestration as currently-considered alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With this notice, the Commission requests specific comments regarding any additional potential alternatives that meet the reasonable-alternative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA public review process for the supplemental EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff will prepare a draft supplemental EIS issued for public comment, will consider all timely comments on the draft, revise as necessary, and then issue a final supplemental EIS. Draft and final SEIS will be available electronically via eLibrary and the Commission's natural gas environmental documents web page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eSubscribed, you will receive email notification when documents are issued. The draft SEIS is expected to open a 45-day comment period when issued; staff will consider only timely comments during that period for revision to the final SEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule for environmental review and decision deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned schedule: draft supplemental EIS issued March 2025 (opening a 45-day comment period); issuance of Notice of Availability of the final supplemental EIS—July 31, 2025; 90-day Federal Authorization Decision Deadline—October 29, 2025; Issuance of Final Order—November 20, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with CEQ regulations, agencies must make schedules for completing NEPA processes publicly available. If the schedule changes, the Commission will provide an additional notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental mailing list composition and update procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's environmental mailing list includes federal, state, and local government representatives and agencies; elected officials; environmental and public interest groups; Native American Tribes; other interested parties; local libraries and newspapers; and affected landowners (as defined in Commission regulations) and anyone who submits comments with a mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change or remove your name/address from the mailing list, email GasProjectAddressChange@ferc.gov with the docket number and correct information, or return the attached 'Mailing List Update Form' (appendix 2). The listed email address cannot accept comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landowner notice regarding easements and eminent domain
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a landowner receiving this notice, a pipeline company representative may contact you to negotiate an easement agreement; you are not required to enter into an agreement. If no agreement is reached and the Commission approves the project, the pipeline company could initiate condemnation proceedings; compensation would be determined by a judge under state law. The Commission does not grant, exercise, or oversee eminent domain authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eminent domain does not apply to NGA section 3 facilities. The courts have exclusive authority over eminent domain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public assistance resources and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Office of Public Participation (OPP) can help the public (landowners, environmental justice communities, Tribal members, and others) access information and navigate Commission processes; contact OPP at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov. For eFiling and eComment assistance contact FERC Online Support at (866) 208-3676 or FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPP can assist with filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing. eSubscription provides automatic notification of filings and document links.
